\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عضله} ('azole)}{عضله ('azole)}]{\fa{عضله} ('azole) — a muscle}

\label{lesson:FA-C495-azole}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for health, then the Persian for to get better.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عضله}}
\textbf{\fa{عضله}} (\emph{'azole}) — \textquotedblleft{}a muscle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{کوهنوردی} \fa{عضله} \fa{های} \fa{پایم} \fa{درد} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ba'd az kuhnavardi 'azolehâ-ye pâyam dard mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After hiking my leg muscles ache.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{'azolehâ}, or the Arabic \emph{'azolât} in formal Persian.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'azole} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ʿaḍala}, 'muscle' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'azole}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'azole}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'azole}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for health, then the Persian for to get better, then say \emph{'azole} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{عضله} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A muscle\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ریه} (riye)}{ریه (riye)}]{\fa{ریه} (riye) — a lung}

\label{lesson:FA-C495-riye}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to get better, then the Persian for a muscle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ریه}}
\textbf{\fa{ریه}} (\emph{riye}) — \textquotedblleft{}a lung\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سیگار} \fa{به} \fa{ریه} \fa{آسیب} \fa{میزند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sigâr be riye âsib mizanad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Smoking harms the lungs.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{riyehâ}. In everyday speech also \emph{shosh}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{riye} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{riʾa}, 'lung' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to get better, then the Persian for a muscle, then say \emph{riye} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کبد} (kabed)}{کبد (kabed)}]{\fa{کبد} (kabed) — the liver}

\label{lesson:FA-C495-kabed}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a muscle, then the Persian for a lung.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کبد}}
\textbf{\fa{کبد}} (\emph{kabed}) — \textquotedblleft{}the liver\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دکتر} \fa{گفت} \fa{کبد} \fa{او} \fa{سالم} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{doktor goft kabed-e u sâlem ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor said his liver is healthy.
\end{quote}

Medical. Everyday Persian also says \emph{jegar}, which is also the liver in kebab.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kabed} is a loan, usually traced to Arabic \emph{kabid}, 'liver'. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کلیه} (kolye)}{کلیه (kolye)}]{\fa{کلیه} (kolye) — a kidney}

\label{lesson:FA-C495-kolye}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a lung, then the Persian for the liver.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{معده} (me'de)}{معده (me'de)}]{\fa{معده} (me'de) — the stomach}

\label{lesson:FA-C495-mede}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the liver, then the Persian for a kidney.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{معده}}
\textbf{\fa{معده}} (\emph{me'de}) — \textquotedblleft{}the stomach\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{غذای} \fa{تند} \fa{معده} \fa{درد} \fa{دارم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ba'd az ghazâ-ye tond me'de dard dâram.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After spicy food I get a stomach ache.
\end{quote}

\emph{shekam} is the belly seen from outside; \emph{me'de} is the organ. \emph{me'de dard} — stomach ache.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{me'de} is a loan, usually traced to Arabic \emph{maʿida}, 'stomach'. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{me'de}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{me'de}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{me'de}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for the liver, then the Persian for a kidney, then say \emph{me'de} again

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 488–495 — a review}

\label{lesson:FA-R495-review-488-495}



\begin{quote}
Say the Persian for clever and witty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item clever, witty, good-natured, generous, caring
  \item polite, rude, touchy, shy, to make fun of
  \item a cold, flu, to sneeze, a sore throat, to run a fever
  \item backache, toothache, to suffer pain, an itch, to hiccup
  \item nausea, to vomit, to faint, to feel faint, to sweat
  \item to examine, pulse, to treat, to get vaccinated, a check-up
  \item to visit, to look after, to nurse, health, to get better
  \item a muscle, a lung, the liver, a kidney, the stomach
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Clever? (\textbf{\fa{باهوش}}.) Witty? (\textbf{\fa{شوخ}}.) Good-natured? (\textbf{\fa{خوش} \fa{اخلاق}}.) Generous? (\textbf{\fa{سخاوتمند}}.) Caring? (\textbf{\fa{دلسوز}}.) Polite? (\textbf{\fa{مودب}}.) Rude? (\textbf{\fa{بیادب}}.) Touchy? (\textbf{\fa{زودرنج}}.) Shy? (\textbf{\fa{کمرو}}.) To make fun of? (\textbf{\fa{مسخره} \fa{کردن}}.) A cold? (\textbf{\fa{سرماخوردگی}}.) Flu? (\textbf{\fa{آنفولانزا}}.) To sneeze? (\textbf{\fa{عطسه} \fa{کردن}}.) A sore throat? (\textbf{\fa{گلودرد}}.) To run a fever? (\textbf{\fa{تب} \fa{کردن}}.) Backache? (\textbf{\fa{کمردرد}}.) Toothache? (\textbf{\fa{دندان} \fa{درد}}.) To suffer pain? (\textbf{\fa{درد} \fa{کشیدن}}.) An itch? (\textbf{\fa{خارش}}.) To hiccup? (\textbf{\fa{سکسکه} \fa{کردن}}.) Nausea? (\textbf{\fa{حالت} \fa{تهوع}}.) To vomit? (\textbf{\fa{استفراغ} \fa{کردن}}.) To faint? (\textbf{\fa{غش} \fa{کردن}}.) To feel faint? (\textbf{\fa{ضعف} \fa{کردن}}.) To sweat? (\textbf{\fa{عرق} \fa{کردن}}.) To examine? (\textbf{\fa{معاینه} \fa{کردن}}.) Pulse? (\textbf{\fa{نبض}}.) To treat? (\textbf{\fa{درمان} \fa{کردن}}.) To get vaccinated? (\textbf{\fa{واکسن} \fa{زدن}}.) A check-up? (\textbf{\fa{چکاپ}}.) To visit? (\textbf{\fa{عیادت} \fa{کردن}}.) To look after? (\textbf{\fa{مراقبت} \fa{کردن}}.) To nurse? (\textbf{\fa{پرستاری} \fa{کردن}}.) Health? (\textbf{\fa{سلامتی}}.) To get better? (\textbf{\fa{خوب} \fa{شدن}}.) A muscle? (\textbf{\fa{عضله}}.) A lung? (\textbf{\fa{ریه}}.) The liver? (\textbf{\fa{کبد}}.) A kidney? (\textbf{\fa{کلیه}}.) The stomach? (\textbf{\fa{معده}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
